# Module Boundary Checklist: Approval Spine

**Purpose**: Interrogate whether the opaque-reference design actually holds Principle I, rather than
appearing to. This is the load-bearing claim of the whole plan — if it fails, the spine is seven
cross-schema violations wearing a service interface.
**Created**: 2026-09-13
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [research.md](../research.md) §1 · [contracts/approval-service.md](../contracts/approval-service.md)

**Note**: Generated by `/speckit-checklist` at the reviewer's request, focused on the Principle I boundary.
**Review Ownership**: Reviewer-owned requirements-quality artifact. Mark `[x]` only when the criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality — not that implementation is done.

## Why this checklist exists

Principle I is NON-NEGOTIABLE: a module's Prisma queries may only touch its own schema, and
cross-module needs go through exported service methods or the event bus. The spine spans `hr`,
`payroll`, `inventory`, `labour`, `projects`, `plant` and `recruitment`. The plan's answer is that
the spine holds only opaque `(entityType, entityId)` references.

That answer is correct *if and only if* the opacity is real in both directions. An opacity that
leaks — a join added later "just for the queue subject", a module reading `ApprovalInstance` to
avoid a service call — converts the design back into the violation it was built to avoid, silently,
and the damage surfaces only at extraction time when it is expensive.

## A. The spine does not read any module

- [ ] CHK001 No spine query, raw or Prisma, references a table outside the `shared` schema.
- [ ] CHK002 No spine table declares a relation or foreign key to a business-module table.
- [ ] CHK003 `ApprovalQueueEntry.subject` and `.href` are supplied by the owning module at submit
      time, not derived by the spine reading the item. This is the specific place the temptation
      will arise, because a queue without subjects is useless and the item is right there.
- [ ] CHK004 No spine code imports a service from a business module in order to *read* item data.
      (Importing to be *called by* is the correct direction.)
- [ ] CHK005 The orphan reconciliation sweep asks each module through its exported service, and does
      not query module tables to find missing items.

## B. No module reads the spine

- [ ] CHK006 No file outside `src/approvals/` accesses `approvalInstance`, `approvalDecision`,
      `approvalChain`, `approvalLevel` or `roleSlotMapping` through Prisma.
- [ ] CHK007 Every module obtains approval state through `ApprovalService`, never by query.
- [ ] CHK008 Quickstart Pass 10's grep is present, runnable, and actually fails when a violation is
      introduced — verify by introducing one deliberately and confirming the grep catches it. A
      guard nobody has seen fail is not known to work.

## C. Completion flows outward, never inward

- [ ] CHK009 The spine never calls a business-module service to announce completion; it emits
      `approval.completed` on the event bus.
- [ ] CHK010 The event payload carries only `(entityType, entityId, companyId, instanceId)` — enough
      for a module to find its own item, nothing that presumes knowledge of the item's shape.
- [ ] CHK011 Each consuming module subscribes and resolves its own item; no shared resolver maps
      entity types to modules, since that map would recreate the coupling in one file.
- [ ] CHK012 The attendance-lock direction is a *synchronous* call into payroll's exported method
      (an answer is needed before the write), while approval invalidation is an *event* (no answer
      needed). Both directions are correct per research.md §5, and neither is the other.

## D. The cost of opacity is actually mitigated

- [ ] CHK013 `abandon(entityType, entityId, reason)` exists and every module that can cancel or
      delete a governed item calls it.
- [ ] CHK014 Items under an incomplete chain are not hard-deleted by any module path.
- [ ] CHK015 An orphaned instance is detectable and reportable, and the report names the module that
      lost the item.
- [ ] CHK016 The absence of referential integrity is documented where a future reader will meet it —
      in the schema comments, not only in research.md.

## E. The boundary survives the second consumer

- [ ] CHK017 Migrating a second module requires no change to the spine's schema. If it does, the
      opaque reference is not general and the design has not been proven by one consumer.
- [ ] CHK018 `statesOf` (batch) is used by every list; `stateOf` appears in no loop. The contract
      names this; the third module to migrate is where it will be got wrong.
- [ ] CHK019 Nothing in the spine special-cases `attendance_exception` — the first consumer must not
      have shaped the mechanism around itself.
- [ ] CHK020 Adding an action type is configuration, not a code change to the spine (spec FR-018a).

## F. Extraction remains possible

- [ ] CHK021 The spine could be lifted into its own service with its interface unchanged, per the
      HLD §10 extraction path Principle I exists to protect. State plainly what would break if it
      were — if the answer is "nothing", the boundary is real.
- [ ] CHK022 No module depends on being in the same transaction as the spine. A decision and the
      item's own state change are separate writes, and the plan says what happens if the second
      fails.

## Notes

- CHK008 and CHK021 are the two that cannot be satisfied by reading code. CHK008 requires
  deliberately breaking the rule to see the guard fire; CHK021 requires reasoning about a migration
  nobody is doing yet. Both are worth the effort, because every other item on this list can pass
  while the boundary is quietly broken.
- CHK022 was raised by this checklist and **has now been answered**: research.md §8 makes
  `ApprovalInstance.state` authoritative, module status derived, the completion handler idempotent,
  and drift detectable by the reconciliation sweep that §1 already required. The item remains
  unchecked because the answer is written but not yet built.
- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the criterion; leave unchecked where evaluation is
  still needed. `/speckit-implement` reads these markers as a gate and must not modify them.
